title: Why does percent mean out of 100?

explain.say: Look at the board. There are 100 dots: 10 rows of 10. The word percent means out of 100. So all 100 dots are 100 percent, the whole thing. How many dots would 1 percent be?

draw.text: Why does percent mean out of 100?

explain.say: Just 1 dot! Now look at this circle cut in half. Half of 100 is 50. So one half is 50 percent. If half your friends walk to school, that is 50 percent of them.
Now the circle is cut into 4 equal slices, and one is shaded. A quarter of 100 is 25. So a quarter is 25 percent. Like 25 cents out of a dollar. What would 3 slices be?
Yes, 75 percent! Now see the bar cut into 10 parts. One tenth is 10 out of 100, so 10 percent. Once you know 10 percent, you can double it for 20 percent.

You are doing great! Here is 80 dollars in percentages: 10 percent is 8, 25 percent is 20, 50 percent is 40. Wow: per cent comes from Latin words meaning for each hundred. Challenge: your phone shows 75 percent. What fraction is left?

faq.q: Where does the word percent come from?
faq.a: From the Latin per centum, which means for each hundred.

faq.q: How do you turn a fraction into a percentage?
faq.a: Make it out of 100, or multiply by 100. A quarter is 25 out of 100, which is 25 percent. Three fifths times 100 is 60 percent.
asks: How do I change 3/5 into a percent?

faq.q: Can a percentage be more than 100?
faq.a: Yes. 100 percent is the whole, so 150 percent is one and a half times as much.

faq.q: How do you find 10 percent of a number?
faq.a: Divide by 10. 10 percent of 80 dollars is 8 dollars. Then you can build other percentages from it.
75 out of 100 is three quarters. So a battery at 75 percent has three quarters left.

facts: Per cent comes from the Latin per centum, meaning for each hundred.

quiz.why: 25 percent is a quarter, and a quarter of 60 is 15.

wrong.1: 25 is the percentage, not the part of 60.

quiz.say: What is 3 tenths as a percentage?
quiz.why: 3 tenths is 30 out of 100, which is 30 percent.

wrong.1: 3 percent is 3 out of 100, ten times smaller.
wrong.2: 0.3 is the decimal, not the percentage.
